purpose: Close the global shutdown ordering defect without changing product scope
changes: All trusted windows prepare by stopping global generation, draining accepted local write actions, flushing owner queues, and draining continuations.
Only after all prepare receipts succeed does main ask its host-bound Stage window to finalize memory ownership and budget writes. Phase and sender must match.
Both phases share the same shutdown ID and absolute deadline. The existing application-wide 8 second watchdog and public shutdown signature remain intact.
A single window close only drains and flushes; it does not dispose the Stage memory owner. Failure keeps the window open and preserves the existing close-failed toast.

PersistenceDrain tracks the real caller Promise and owner Pinia action hook for a narrow write-action allowlist, including local secure-save prefixes that occur before synced RPC. It retains no action arguments, results, or errors.
Pending-at-close failures yield persisted:false; completed historical semantic errors do not poison later attempts. A failed attempt is reset only when host aborts that close.
